To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the flicker noise is the dominant noise in the GPS time-series and it prevails over the white noise.

for the Sudeten area the white plus flickers plus random walk noise model is the most suitable for the GPS time series, the flicker noise is prevailing over other kinds of power-law noises, and the uncertainties of permanent stations velocities are at the level of a few mm/year.

the permanent GPS velocities uncertainties in the Sudeten area are underestimated by 1-10 times if we assume the white noise only model and by 10 times if we apply the combination of the power-law and white noises.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed analysis of the GPS-derived time series from the area of the Sudeten.
the analysis of GPS time series from permanent stations in the Sudeten.
the uncertainties of permanent stations velocity and their origin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the white noise model is not sufficient to describe the GPS time series, while the flickering noise prevails over the other kinds of noise.
the white noise is present in the GPS time-series and it is the only one that should be considered when estimating the permanent stations velocities.
the white noise is not sufficient to describe the stochastic part of geodetic time series and that it is necessary to take into account the power-law noise.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the permanent stations velocities should not be estimated using the white noise model, because it leads to the under-estimation of the uncertainties.
the flicker noise is the dominant one in the GPS coordinate time series, which is confirmed by the spectral index of the power-law noise and its amplitude.
the permanent GPS station velocities are not as stable as we would expect, and the white noise model is not the best one for the GPS coordinate time series.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the white plus flickering noise model is the best one in describing the time series of the geodetic coordinates, and it is the most suitable to be used in further geodetic applications, such as the realization of the kinematic reference frames or geodynamic interpretations.
the flicker noise should be considered in the GPS time-series modeling, which will lead to the proper estimation of velocity uncertainties.
the white noise model is not sufficient to estimate the permanent station velocity uncertainties.
